summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue was modest at INR182 crore, while a INR2,205 crore HAL Uttam Radar order lifted the total order book to about INR4,300 crore.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 as modest on revenue and profitability, blaming customer approval delays and last-stage technical issues that it expects to normalise in coming quarters. Q1 order inflow was INR185 crore, in line with guidance. The July receipt of the INR2,205 crore HAL Uttam Radar subsystem order (about INR1,870 crore ex-GST) roughly doubled the order book. Management reiterated FY27 revenue of about INR1,350 crore (guided as more than 15-20% growth) and flagged a planned demerger of the Space and Weather divisions from April 1, 2027.

segments.name: Defence (Uttam Radar, HAL)
segments.commentary: Largest order in company history: about INR2,205 crore from HAL for critical subsystems for Uttam Radar, with a 5-year execution window. Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027, about 14 months from order date.

segments.name: Space, Metrology and Hydrology
segments.commentary: About 34% of the standalone order book. Management guided INR120-150 crore of FY27 revenue from space. Space and Weather is to be demerged as a separate listed entity, with first-year standalone revenue guided at INR300-plus crore and at least 18-20% PBT margin.

segments.name: Joint venture (Astra Rafael Comsys)
segments.commentary: Order book INR836 crore; FY27 booking target INR360 crore. Management expects INR500-750 crore of further ARC orders over the forecast period.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target about INR1,350 crore, plus or minus INR25 crore; growth stated as more than 15%, with 15-20% given in Q&A.
FY28 revenue about INR1,600 crore, plus or minus INR50 crore, with growth of 15-18%.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR1,600 crore, excluding the Uttam order; management said it may be improved over the next few quarters.
Over 5 years, management expects at least 6-7x FY26 revenue. It sees order intake of INR8,000-9,000 crore over 3-4 years, excluding chip sales, counter-UAV, EM wall, exports and BrahMos NG.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be similar to FY26, with a positive delta increase; no long-term margin guidance given.
Management said it expects the Q3 and Q4 working capital position to be broadly similar to FY26, and it has no plan to dilute equity for working capital.
capex_capacity: Uttam Radar: Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027; roughly 25+ numbers per year thereafter; management said total quantity could be executed by FY31.
Own satellite to be launched within the first 6 months after the Space and Weather entity lists; part of a planned satellite constellation.
Management said production lines and teams are fully ready for large-scale execution; investment in automated process engineering and infrastructure is ongoing.
Migration to SAP/HANA completed; standalone accounting for the space business has run from the start of the year.
Two complete radars of own IP and one drone-mounted electronic intelligence product are targeted for around Diwali 2026.
demand_pricing: AMCA AAAU: company is L1 and BEL is L2 for the active antenna array unit development, with a contract expected in about a month. Management did not disclose the quantum; the AMCA radar DcPP RFP has 3 shortlisted consortium partners.

Tejas Mk1A EW: AATRU subsystem already qualified; the EW suite is in final qualification, after which production orders follow. Management expects about INR500-600 crore of additional orders from these programmes.
Su-30 upgrades (Virupaksha, Angad): Tier 1 radar and Tier 2 EW role; management expects about INR3,000 crore of orders over the forecast period.
QRSAM: expects INR700-800 crore of orders for the first 3 regiments; part of the existing INR4,300 crore book is expected before year-end.
Shatrughat and Samaghat (P-75I): management expects INR100-120 crore of production orders from BEL for the two programmes combined.
BrahMos: supplies gimbal-based RF seeker components and telemetry products; a new-generation (NG) seeker is in development. Upside from NG is not in the order inflow projections.
Exports: a couple of BTS orders executed and prototypes given for qualification; MMIC component leads from US and Europe, with sizable orders possibly taking about 2 more years.

qa_highlights.question: Which top-line growth target is correct: 10-15% (press release) or 15-20% (presentation)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the correct target is in excess of 15%, i.e. 15-20% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the year-end order book target?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding Uttam, management reiterated order booking of about INR1,600 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is EW (Tejas, Su-30) and LCH content in the order inflow projections?
qa_highlights.answer: Angad and some LCH subsystems are included in the 4-year projections. Tejas Mk1A is additional, around INR500-600 crore. Management said none of the EM wall or counter-UAV revenue is in its numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to positive cash at the end of FY26, which kept overdraft utilisation in Q1 minimal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uttam execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall execution is about 5 years, with total completion before FY32 and possibly by FY31; Phase 1 of 12 numbers is due by September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What margin guidance is available for new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to margins, citing product mix and lifecycle economics. It expects margins to be as healthy as the current business, or nearly so.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 6-7x five-year revenue target based on the defence business only?
qa_highlights.answer: The order visibility excludes space, apart from the existing book. Management said the 6-7x is against the combined FY26 base of INR1,057 crore, since the demerger has not yet happened.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue decline and was there deferred revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited inspection and specification-proof delays, development-cycle issues and supply-chain issues that pushed some programmes out of Q1. It expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger and said quarterly numbers are internal estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital moderate further in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant change versus FY26 is expected; Q1 and early Q2 are seasonally better and pressure rises in Q3 and Q4. Management ruled out equity dilution for working capital.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 revenue of INR182 crore was described as modest; management attributes shortfall to inspection, specification-proof, development-cycle and supply-chain delays and expects Q3 and Q4 to carry the year, so watch whether H2 execution delivers the INR1,350 crore FY27 target (+/-INR25 crore).

Execution load on the INR2,205 crore Uttam Radar order: Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027 and roughly 25+ numbers per year thereafter; supply chains are stretched and management flagged cross-border supply risk.

Working capital: management expects Q3 and Q4 pressure to build and no significant change versus FY26; it ruled out equity dilution for working capital, so monitor receivables and operating cash flow at the end-Q3 update.

Order inflow visibility rests on unawarded programmes (AMCA AAAU where the company is L1 with contract expected in about a month, QRSAM, Su-30 Virupaksha/Angad, Tejas Mk1A EW, P-75I); none of the EM wall, counter-UAV, chip, export or BrahMos NG upside is in numbers.

Space and Weather demerger from April 1, 2027: details on leadership, plans, satellite launch and the INR300-plus crore first-year revenue guidance remain to be shared over the next few quarters; watch for structure and shareholder-ratio clarity.

Long-term 5-year 6-7x revenue ambition and INR8,000-9,000 crore order intake ambition were questioned by analysts (ICICI Securities on cumulative execution); management said it would clarify one-to-one, so treat as unverified until tracked.
key_quotes: The revenue and profitability were moderate -- modest, I should say, primarily due to temporary delays in customer approvals and closing some of the last stage technical issues, which are expected to normalize in the coming quarters.

So we have to keep that distinction in mind or AEW&C Mk-2, where we are part of the supply chain or the supply chain for Mk1, where we will have, I think, at least 25%, if not more, of the designated supply chain
But we don't want to commit to you on the margins because there are a lot of factors which will come into play from incremental products, number one.
Till we have accretive nonorganic opportunities, we will not dilute for working capital.
Our quarterly numbers are our internal numbers, which we are constantly fine-tuning.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the order book and long-term ambitions, particularly the Uttam Radar win and FY27 guidance, but openly cautious and defensive on Q1 performance, attributing the modest revenue to temporary approval and technical delays. It was evasive on new-product margins, declining to commit beyond "as healthy as the current business, if not as healthy," and on quarterly numbers, which it called internal estimates.
